title: Bekhorot 42
description: Is a tumtum certainly male or female, or a creature of its own kind? Seven challenges are answered with “omit the tumtum” or, once, by swapping it for an orphan; then the question moves to animals that urinate from the female place, and to the tumtum’s marriage, ḥalitza and levirate marriage.
topics: ✂️ “Omit the tumtum”: seven challenges to Rav Ḥisda, from valuations, offerings, birds and substitutes
🐣 Swap the tumtum for an orphan to keep Rabbi Elazar’s count of five
⚖️ Rabbi Shimon ben Yehuda: does a tumtum that urinates from the female place count as female?
🤔 Rabbi Yoḥanan wonders at Rabbi Elazar’s ruling; Reish Lakish: a tumtum is uncertain only in a person
🔄 “Since it has changed, it has changed”: Rav Oshaya, Abaye, and the sons of Avin
💍 A tumtum’s betrothal, ḥalitza and levirate marriage: Rabbi Akiva, Rabbi Eliezer, Rabbi Yehuda and his son Rabbi Yosei

a1.he: אַלְּמָה תַּנְיָא: ״הַזָּכָר״ — וְלֹא טוּמְטוּם וְאַנְדְּרוֹגִינוֹס! סְמִי מִיכָּן טוּמְטוּם.

a2.he: תָּא שְׁמַע: יָכוֹל לֹא יְהֵא בְּעֵרֶךְ אִישׁ, אֲבָל יְהֵא בְּעֵרֶךְ אִשָּׁה? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״הַזָּכָר... אִם נְקֵבָה״, וְלֹא טוּמְטוּם וְאַנְדְּרוֹגִינוֹס! סְמִי מִיכָּן טוּמְטוּם.

a3.he: תָּא שְׁמַע: ״אִם זָכָר אִם נְקֵבָה״ — זָכָר וַדַּאי נְקֵבָה וַדָּאִית, וְלֹא טוּמְטוּם וְאַנְדְּרוֹגִינוֹס. סְמִי מִיכָּן טוּמְטוּם.

a4.he: תָּא שְׁמַע: ״הַזָּכָר״ — וְלֹא נְקֵבָה. כְּשֶׁהוּא אוֹמֵר לְמַטָּהּ ״זָכָר״, שֶׁאֵין תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר; מָה תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר? לְהוֹצִיא טוּמְטוּם וְאַנְדְּרוֹגִינוֹס. סְמִי מִיכָּן טוּמְטוּם.

a5.he: תָּא שְׁמַע: הַנֶּעֱבָד, וְהַמּוּקְצֶה, וְהָאֶתְנַן, וְהַמְּחִיר, וְטוּמְטוּם וְאַנְדְּרוֹגִינוֹס — כּוּלָּן מְטַמְּאִין בְּגָדִים אַבֵּית הַבְּלִיעָה.

a6.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: טוּמְטוּם וְאַנְדְּרוֹגִינוֹס אֵין מְטַמְּאִין בְּגָדִים אַבֵּית הַבְּלִיעָה, שֶׁהָיָה רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: כׇּל מָקוֹם שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״זָכָר וּנְקֵבָה״ אַתָּה מוֹצִיא טוּמְטוּם וְאַנְדְּרוֹגִינוֹס מִבֵּינֵיהֶם.

a7.he: וְעוֹף, הוֹאִיל וְלֹא נֶאֱמַר בּוֹ ״זָכָר וּנְקֵבָה״, אֵין אַתָּה מוֹצִיא טוּמְטוּם וְאַנְדְּרוֹגִינוֹס מִבֵּינֵיהֶם! סְמִי מִיכָּן טוּמְטוּם.

a8.he: תָּא שְׁמַע: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר: הַטְּרֵיפָה, וְהַכִּלְאַיִם, וְיוֹצֵא דּוֹפֶן, טוּמְטוּם וְאַנְדְּרוֹגִינוֹס — לֹא קְדוֹשִׁים וְלֹא מַקְדִּישִׁין.

a9.he: וְאָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: לֹא קְדוֹשִׁים בִּתְמוּרָה, וְלֹא מַקְדִּישִׁין לַעֲשׂוֹת תְּמוּרָה! סְמִי מִיכָּן טוּמְטוּם.

a10.he: תָּא שְׁמַע: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר: חֲמִשָּׁה לֹא קְדוֹשִׁים וְלֹא מַקְדִּישִׁין, וְאֵלּוּ הֵן: הַטְּרֵיפָה, וְהַכִּלְאַיִם, וְיוֹצֵא דּוֹפֶן, וְטוּמְטוּם, וְאַנְדְּרוֹגִינוֹס. וְכִי תֵּימָא הָכָא נָמֵי סְמִי מִיכָּן טוּמְטוּם — הָווּ לְהוּ אַרְבָּעָה! אַפֵּיק טוּמְטוּם, וְעָיֵיל יָתוֹם.

a11.he: לֵימָא כְּתַנָּאֵי? רַבִּי אִילְעַאי אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל: אַנְדְּרוֹגִינוֹס בְּכוֹר הוּא וּמוּמוֹ עִמּוֹ, וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: אֵין קְדוּשָּׁה חָלָה עָלָיו. רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן: הֲרֵי הוּא אוֹמֵר ״הַזָּכָר״, וְכׇל מָקוֹם שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״זָכָר״ אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא לְהוֹצִיא טוּמְטוּם וְאַנְדְּרוֹגִינוֹס.

a12.he: וְכִי תֵּימָא: סְמִי מִיכָּן טוּמְטוּם, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יְהוּדָה הַיְינוּ רַבָּנַן! אֶלָּא לָאו טוּמְטוּם אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ, דְּתַנָּא קַמָּא סָבַר: אֵין קְדוּשָּׁה חָלָה עָלָיו אַאַנְדְּרוֹגִינוֹס, אֲבָל טוּמְטוּם סְפֵיקָא הוּא וְקָדוֹשׁ מִסְּפֵיקָא, וַאֲתָא רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן

b1.he: בֶּן יְהוּדָה לְמֵימַר: טוּמְטוּם בְּרִיָּה הוּא וְלֹא קָדוֹשׁ! לָא, דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא טוּמְטוּם בִּבְרִיָּה לָא מְסַפְּקָא, זָכָר וּנְקֵבָה הוּא דִּמְסַפְּקָא.

b2.he: מֵטִיל מַיִם בִּמְקוֹם זַכְרוּת — דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי דְּזָכָר הוּא, כִּי פְּלִיגִי בְּמֵטִיל מַיִם בְּמָקוֹם נַקְבוּת: מָר סָבַר חָיְישִׁינַן שֶׁמָּא נֶהֶפְכָה זַכְרוּתוֹ לְנַקְבוּתוֹ, וּמַר סָבַר לָא חָיְישִׁינַן. כִּי הָא דְּהוֹרָה רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: בִּבְהֵמָה מֵטִיל מַיִם בְּמָקוֹם נַקְבוּת — חוּלִּין.

b3.he: תָּהֵי בַּהּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: מַאן דְּלָא חָשׁ לְתַנָּא קַמָּא וּלְרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל? וְלֵימָא רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן נָמֵי: מַאן דְּלָא חָשׁ לְרַבָּנַן בָּתְרָאֵי? דְּאָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: מַחֲלוֹקֶת בְּאַנְדְּרוֹגִינוֹס, אֲבָל בְּטוּמְטוּם — דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל סְפֵיקָא!

b4.he: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן לָא סְבִירָא לֵיהּ דְּרַב חִסְדָּא, אִי לָא סְבִירָא לֵיהּ, לֵימָא הוּא דְּאָמַר כְּרַבָּנַן בָּתְרָאֵי? הָכִי נָמֵי קָאָמַר: מַאן שָׁבֵיק תְּרֵי וְעָבֵיד כְּחַד!

b5.he: וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר כְּמַאן סָבְרַהּ? כִּי הָא דְּאָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ: לֹא אָמְרוּ טוּמְטוּם סָפֵק אֶלָּא בְּאָדָם, הוֹאִיל וְזַכְרוּתוֹ וְנַקְבוּתוֹ בְּמָקוֹם אֶחָד, אֲבָל בְּהֵמָה — מֵטִיל מַיִם בְּמָקוֹם זַכְרוּת זָכָר, מֵטִיל מַיִם בְּמָקוֹם נַקְבוּת נְקֵבָה.

b6.he: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב אוֹשַׁעְיָא: וְלֵיחוּשׁ שֶׁמָּא נֶהֶפְכָה זַכְרוּתוֹ לְנַקְבוּתוֹ! אֲמַר לֵיהּ: כְּמַאן? כְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר דְּחָיֵישׁ לְמִיעוּטָא?!

b7.he: אַבָּיֵי בַּר אָבִין וְרַב חֲנַנְיָא בַּר אָבִין דְאָמְרִי תַּרְוַיְיהוּ: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא רַבָּנַן, הוֹאִיל וְאִישְׁתַּנִּי אִישְׁתַּנִּי. אִית דְּאָמַר אִישְׁתַּנִּי, וְאִית דְּאָמַר לָא אִישְׁתַּנִּי.

b8.he: לֵימָא אִישְׁתַּנִּי וְלָא אִישְׁתַּנִּי תַּנָּאֵי? דְּתַנְיָא: טוּמְטוּם שֶׁקִּידֵּשׁ — קִדּוּשָׁיו קִדּוּשִׁין, נִתְקַדֵּשׁ — קִדּוּשָׁיו קִדּוּשִׁין.

b9.he: וְחוֹלֵץ, וְחוֹלְצִין לְאִשְׁתּוֹ, וּמְיַבְּמִים לְאִשְׁתּוֹ. וְתַנְיָא אִידַּךְ: אֵשֶׁת טוּמְטוּם חוֹלֶצֶת וְלֹא מִתְיַיבֶּמֶת.

b10.he: סַבְרוּהָ, דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא כְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא, דְּאָמַר: סְרִיס חַמָּה לֹא חוֹלֵץ וְלֹא מְיַיבֵּם.

b11.he: מַאי לָאו בְּהָא קָמִיפַּלְגִי, דְּמַאן דְּאָמַר חוֹלֵץ, וְחוֹלְצִין לְאִשְׁתּוֹ וּמְיַבְּמִים אֶת אִשְׁתּוֹ, לָא אָמְרִינַן הוֹאִיל וְאִישְׁתַּנִּי אִישְׁתַּנִּי;

b12.he: וּמַאן דְּאָמַר חוֹלֶצֶת וְלֹא מִתְיַיבֶּמֶת, אָמְרִינַן הוֹאִיל וְאִישְׁתַּנִּי אִישְׁתַּנִּי?

b13.he: לָא, דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא אָמְרִינַן הוֹאִיל וְאִישְׁתַּנִּי אִישְׁתַּנִּי, הָא רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר, וְהָא רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא.

b14.he: וּמַאן תַּנָּא אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא? אִילֵימָא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה — הָא וַדַּאי סָרִיס מְשַׁוֵּי לֵיהּ!

b15.he: דִּתְנַן, רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: טוּמְטוּם שֶׁנִּקְרַע וְנִמְצָא זָכָר — הֲרֵי זֶה לֹא יַחְלוֹץ, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהוּא כְּסָרִיס!

b16.he: אֶלָּא רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה הִיא, דְּתַנְיָא: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: טוּמְטוּם לֹא חוֹלֵץ, שֶׁמָּא יִקָּרַע וְיִמָּצֵא סָרִיס חַמָּה.

b17.he: אַטּוּ כֹּל דְּמִיקְּרַע זָכָר מִשְׁתְּכַח, נְקֵבָה לָא מִשְׁתְּכַח? שֶׁמָּא קָאָמַר, שֶׁמָּא יִקָּרַע וְיִמָּצֵא נְקֵבָה.

b18.he: אִי נָמֵי זָכָר נָמֵי, שֶׁמָּא יִמָּצֵא סָרִיס חַמָּה. מַאי בֵּינַיְיהוּ? אָמַר רָבָא:

messages.text: Continued from 41b. Rav Ḥisda said everyone agrees a tumtum is an uncertain case: certainly male or female, we just don’t know which. Rava challenged him: then it should be valuated.
Why, then, is it taught in a baraita that the verse: “Then your valuation shall be for the male”, includes one whose status as a male is certain but not a tumtum or a hermaphrodite?

verse.he: וְהָיָה עֶרְכְּךָ הַזָּכָר מִבֶּן עֶשְׂרִים שָׁנָה וְעַד בֶּן־שִׁשִּׁים שָׁנָה וְהָיָה עֶרְכְּךָ חֲמִשִּׁים שֶׁקֶל כֶּסֶף בְּשֶׁקֶל הַקֹּדֶשׁ׃
verse.en: the following scale shall apply: If it is a male from twenty to sixty years of age, the equivalent is fifty shekels of silver by the sanctuary weight;

notes.he: והיה ערכך הזכר ומריבויא דה"א נפקא לן ולא טומטום:
notes.en: Why then is it taught “the male”: “then your valuation shall be: the male.” We derive it from the extra “the”: and not a tumtum.

notes.dh: אלמה תניא הזכר ולא טומטום ואנדרוגינוס
notes.he: מייתורא קדריש אבל מזכר לחודיה לא קממעט כדאמר בסוף המפלת (נדה דף כח:) וכר' יהודה אתיא כדמוכח בשבת בסוף פרק אם לא הביא כלי (דף קלו:) דאמר רב חסדא לא לכל א"ר יהודה אנדרוגינוס זכר הוא שאם אתה אומר כן בערכין יערך ותניא הזכר ולא טומטום כו' פירוש וסתם ספרא ר' יהודה היא (לקמן בכורות דף סא.) וקאמר ר"נ בר יצחק אף אנן נמי תנינא דקא"ר יהודה פוסל באשה ואנדרוגינוס לקידוש מי חטאת ומאי שנא גבי מילה דכתיב (בראשית יז) המול לכם כל זכר ויש לתמוה מאי שנא דבערכין צריך ייתור למעט אנדרוגינוס ובקידוש לא צריך מיעוט אלא ממעטינן ליה מהיכא דממעטינן אשה מונתן ולא ונתנה כדאמרינן בפרק טרף בקלפי (יומא דף מג.) ובמילה אדרבה צריך יתור לרבותן לדין זכר ומיהו מקידוש הוה מצינן למימר דשמא איכא מיעוט אבל מילה קשיא וי"ל דקסבר ר' יהודה אנדרוגינוס מוצא מכלל זכר בלא שום מיעוט מסברא ולהכי פסל ליה קדוש ולענין מילה צריך ייתורא דכל זכר לריבויא והא דבעי מיעוטא בערכין היינו משום דמסברא הייתי מעמידו לכל הפחות בערך נקבה אי לאו דמעטיה מנקבה (לאוקומיה בערך) וברייתא דעולה דלעיל דאיצטריך קרא למעוטי מזכר לאו כר' יהודה אע"ג דסתם סיפרא היא דהא בקידוש פוסלו ר' יהודה בלא שום ייתור ומ"מ פשיטא ליה דההיא דערכין (דף ד.) ר' יהודה כל כמה דאיכא לאוקומיה סתם סיפרא כוותיה מוקמינן ועוד תניא בהדיא בפ"ק דערכין (דף ה:) דר' יהודה אומר הטומטום ואנדרוגינוס מעריכין אבל לא נערכין ומיהו קשה לפי שיטה שפירשתי מפרק הערל (יבמות דף עב:) דמשמע התם דלא פסיל ליה ר' יהודה לענין קדוש אלא מספק דהוי ספק איש ספק אשה דתניא ר' יהודה אומר אף אנדרוגינוס שקדש קדושו פסול מפני שהוא ספק אשה ואשה פסולה לקדש ונראה לפרש דספק הוא לר' יהודה ולענין מילה אי כאשה גמורה ריבהו הכתוב מכל זכר דמשמע כל זכרות ולענין ערכין מעטו הכתוב מערך איש ואשה לפי שהוא משונה:
notes.en: In brief: Tosafot note that the exclusion comes from the extra word, not from “male” alone (Niddah 28b), and that this baraita follows Rabbi Yehuda, as shown in Shabbat 136b, where Rav Ḥisda says Rabbi Yehuda did not call a hermaphrodite male in every respect, for then it would be valuated, and an unattributed Sifra is Rabbi Yehuda. They ask why Rabbi Yehuda needs an extra word to exclude a hermaphrodite from valuations, when he disqualifies it from sanctifying the water of the red heifer with no verse, and includes it in circumcision only from “every male.” They answer that by reasoning alone Rabbi Yehuda already places a hermaphrodite outside “male”: circumcision needs a verse to include it, and valuations need one so that we do not value it at least as a woman. Finally, in light of Yevamot 72b, where Rabbi Yehuda disqualifies it as “perhaps a woman,” they suggest that for him it is a doubt: circumcision includes it as a full male, and valuations exclude it as anomalous. Open on Sefaria for the full text.

messages.text: Omit from this baraita the mention of a tumtum, as it is referring only to a hermaphrodite, which is a distinct entity.
messages.quote: but not a tumtum or a hermaphrodite

messages.text: Come and hear the continuation of that baraita:

One might have thought that these shall not be valuated according to the valuation of a man, but they shall be valuated according to the valuation of a woman. Therefore, the verse states: “The male,” and in the following verse it states: “And if she is a female, then your valuation shall be thirty shekels”, indicating only one whose status as a male or female is certain, but not a tumtum or a hermaphrodite, which are categorized as neither male nor female.

verse.he: וְאִם־נְקֵבָה הִוא וְהָיָה עֶרְכְּךָ שְׁלֹשִׁים שָׁקֶל׃
verse.en: if it is a female, the equivalent is thirty shekels.

notes.he: אין שוין כדמפרש בפ' בהר סיני:
notes.en: A man’s valuation and a woman’s are not equal, as explained in the section of Behar Sinai.

notes.he: מריבויא דאם נפקא לן ולא טומטום משום ספיקא לא ממעיט ליה קרא דספיקא קמי שמיא ליכא אלא ודאי משום בריה ממעיט ליה:
notes.en: “If a female”: we derive it from the extra “if”: and not a tumtum. The verse does not exclude it because of uncertainty, since before Heaven there is no uncertainty; it must be excluding it as a creature of its own kind.

notes.he: דאין מחמירין עליו מספיקא:
notes.en: One might think it shall not be by a man’s valuation: since we do not impose the stricter amount out of doubt.

notes.he: אבל יהא בערך אשה דערכה פחות משל איש:
notes.en: But it shall be by a woman’s valuation, since hers is less than a man’s.

messages.text: Omit from this baraita the mention of a tumtum, as it is referring only to a hermaphrodite.
messages.quote: but not a tumtum or a hermaphrodite

notes.he: מקרא לא ממעט אלא אנדרוגינוס ומשום בריה אבל טומטום נערך ולחומרא נערך כזכר:
notes.en: Omit the tumtum from here: the verse excludes only the hermaphrodite, as a creature of its own kind. A tumtum is valuated, and stringently, as a male.

notes.he: דטומטום נערך מספיקא:
notes.en: Omit the tumtum from here: a tumtum is valuated out of uncertainty.

messages.text: Come and hear a baraita discussing the peace offering, with regard to which it states:
“Whether male or female”. This indicates: Only a definite male or a definite female, but not a tumtum or a hermaphrodite.

verse.he: וְאִם־זֶבַח שְׁלָמִים קׇרְבָּנוֹ אִם מִן־הַבָּקָר הוּא מַקְרִיב אִם־זָכָר אִם־נְקֵבָה תָּמִים יַקְרִיבֶנּוּ לִפְנֵי יְהֹוָה׃
verse.en:
If your offering is a sacrifice of well-being uncertain.—
If you offer of the herd, whether a male or a female, you shall bring before GOD one without blemish.

notes.he: בשלמים כתיב (ויקרא ז) ומשום ספק לא ממעט קרא ועוד בין זכר בין נקבה כשר לשלמים אלא ודאי בריה הוא:
notes.en: “Whether male or female” is written of the peace offering. A verse does not exclude because of uncertainty; and besides, male and female are both fit for a peace offering. So it must be a creature of its own kind.

notes.he: דכתיב גבי שלמים:
notes.en: “Whether male or female”: as written of the peace offering.

messages.text: Omit from this baraita the mention of a tumtum.
messages.quote: but not a tumtum or a hermaphrodite

notes.he: סמי מיכן טומטום דהא קדיש מספיקא:
notes.en: Omit the tumtum from here, since it is sacred out of uncertainty.

messages.text: Come and hear a baraita:

It states with regard to a burnt offering from cattle: “A male”, from which it can be inferred: But not a female. When it says below, with regard to a burnt offering from sheep: “A male” a second time, it is difficult to understand, as there is no need for the verse to state this. Why must the verse state “a male” again? This serves to exclude a tumtum and a hermaphrodite, which are disqualified as burnt offerings.

verse.he: וְאִם־מִן־הַצֹּאן קׇרְבָּנוֹ מִן־הַכְּשָׂבִים אוֹ מִן־הָעִזִּים לְעֹלָה זָכָר תָּמִים יַקְרִיבֶנּוּ׃
verse.en: If your offering for a burnt offering is from the flock, of sheep or of goats, you shall make your offering a male without blemish.

notes.he: דהיינו הך דגבי עולה דפרישית לעיל להוציא טומטום ומדמעטיה קרא בריה הוא דמשום ספק לא ממעט קרא: הרובע ל"ג דלא שייך בעופות:
notes.en: “A male, and not a female”: this is the one about the burnt offering I explained above, which excludes a tumtum. Since the verse excluded it, it is a creature of its own kind, as a verse does not exclude because of uncertainty. (In the next baraita we do not read “the one that copulated,” since that does not apply to birds.)

notes.he: דטומטום נמי בריה הוא:
notes.en: To exclude a tumtum and a hermaphrodite: since a tumtum too is a creature of its own kind.

messages.text: Omit from this baraita the mention of a tumtum.
messages.quote: to exclude a tumtum and a hermaphrodite

messages.text: Come and hear a baraita discussing the halakhot of ritual impurity imparted by a bird in the throat: Any bird that was not slaughtered in the proper manner, i.e., in its neck with a knife, has the status of a carcass. This carcass renders the one who eats it impure when it is in his throat. Bird offerings, which are killed by pinching the nape of the neck with a fingernail, are the exception to this principle, and they do not impart impurity.

With regard to a bird that is worshipped as a deity, or one set aside for idol worship, or one given as payment to a prostitute, or one that was given as the price of a dog, and similarly with regard to a bird that is a tumtum or a hermaphrodite, if one killed any of them by pinching, they are ritually impure, as they are disqualified as offerings, and the pinching does not purify them. Therefore, they all render a person and the garments he is wearing ritually impure if an olive-bulk of them comes into contact with the throat while eating.

notes.he: כולה בקרבנות דעופות קמיירי:
notes.en: That is worshipped: the whole baraita speaks of bird offerings.

notes.he: כשאר נבלת עוף טהור דמליקתו אינה מליקה והוי נבילה ואי לאו בריה הוא אמאי אינה מליקה מה נפשך אם זכר הוא כשר ואם נקבה הרי כשר דהא בעופות לא חלק הכתוב ועוד מדר"א איכא לאותוביה דקאמר כל מקום שאתה מוצא זכר ונקבה אתה מוציא טומטום ספיקא מי ממעט ליה קרא אלא ודאי בריה הוא והיכא דמעטיה מעטיה אבל בעופות דלא מעטיה לא מעטיה:
notes.en: They render garments impure in the throat: like any carcass of a kosher bird, since its pinching is no valid pinching and it is a carcass. If it were not a creature of its own kind, why would its pinching be invalid? Either way: if it is male it is fit, and if female it is fit, since with birds the Torah made no distinction. And there is a further challenge from Rabbi Eliezer, who says “wherever you find male and female, you exclude a tumtum”: would a verse exclude an uncertainty? It must be a creature of its own kind; where the Torah excluded it, it is excluded, and with birds, where it did not, it is not.

notes.he: והמוקצה לע"ז והאתנן והמחיר. הני כולהו בתורים ובני יונה מיירי דאי מלקן לא חל עלייהו קדושת מזבח אלא נבילה הווין ומטמא בגדים אבית הבליעה. אלמא דטומטום לא קדיש למזבח:
notes.en: That is worshipped as an idol, set aside for idol worship, a prostitute’s payment and the price of a dog: all these speak of turtledoves and young pigeons. If one pinched them, the sanctity of the altar does not take effect on them; they are carcasses and render garments impure in the throat. Evidently a tumtum is not sacred for the altar.

messages.text: If one pinched the neck of a tumtum or a hermaphrodite, it does not render the person and the garments he is wearing ritually impure when they are in the throat, as they are in fact fit to be sacrificed.

notes.dh: טומטום ואנדרוגינוס אין מטמאין בגדים אבית הבליעה
notes.he: ה"ה דלהקרבה נמי כשרין כדמפרש טעמא אלא איידי דנקט ת"ק טמא נקט ר"א אין מטמאין:
notes.en: A tumtum and a hermaphrodite do not render garments impure in the throat: the same applies to offering them, which is permitted, as the reason explains. But since the first tanna said “impure,” Rabbi Eliezer said “do not render impure.”

messages.text: Wherever it is stated explicitly in the Torah: “Male,” and: “Female,” you should exclude a tumtum and a hermaphrodite from among them, as their status is uncertain. This applies to animal offerings, with regard to which the Torah states “male” and “female.”

But in the case of a bird offering, since “male” and “female” are not stated with regard to it, but simply doves and pigeons are stated with regard to it, you do not exclude a tumtum and a hermaphrodite from among them, as they are fit for the altar.
Now if a tumtum is considered either definitely a male or a female, then why does the first tanna disqualify it from being sacrificed? Omit from this baraita the mention of a tumtum.

notes.he: סמי מכאן טומטום:
notes.en: Omit the tumtum from here.

messages.text: Come and hear that

An animal with a condition that will cause it to die within twelve months [tereifa], and prohibited diverse kinds of livestock, and an animal born by caesarean section, and an animal that is a tumtum or a hermaphrodite do not become consecrated and do not render another animal consecrated in their place.

They do not become consecrated by substitution, i.e., if one sought to substitute one of these animals for a sacrificial animal, it does not become sacred. And if one of these was born to a sacrificial animal, they do not render a non-sacred animal consecrated in a case where one wanted to render it a substitute for them.
messages.quote: do not become consecrated and do not render another animal consecrated

notes.he: כלומר אפילו תמורה שחלה על בעל מום קבוע אינה חלה עליהן וטעמא מפרש במסכת תמורה בפרק יש בקרבנות (תמורה דף יז.):
notes.en: They do not become consecrated by substitution: that is, even substitution, which takes effect on an animal with a permanent blemish, does not take effect on them. The reason is explained in tractate Temurah, chapter Yesh BaKorbanot (17a).

notes.he: שאם הם קדושין אין עושין תמורה והיכי דמי שהן עצמן קדושין כגון שהיו ולדות קדשים דקדשי אגב אמן ואי טומטום ספק הוא אמאי לא קדוש ממה נפשך:
notes.en: And they do not render consecrated as substitutes: if they are sacred, they cannot make a substitute. How could they themselves be sacred? For example, if they were offspring of consecrated animals, sacred through their mothers. And if a tumtum is an uncertainty, why is it not sacred, either way?

notes.he: שאם רצה לעשותם תמורת קדשים אינן קדישין במקומן ואם הקדישן ורצה להמירן בבהמ' חולין לא מקדישין לא אלימי למיתפס תמורתן:
notes.en: They do not become consecrated by substitution: if one wanted to make them substitutes for consecrated animals, they do not become sacred in their place. And if he consecrated them and wanted to exchange them for a non-sacred animal, they do not consecrate it; they are not strong enough for their substitute to take hold.

messages.text: And if a tumtum is either a male or female, why would it not become consecrated and render another animal consecrated? Omit from this baraita the mention of a tumtum.
Come and hear a slightly different version of that baraita.

There are five types of animals that do not become consecrated and do not render another animal consecrated, and they are: A tereifa, and prohibited diverse kinds of livestock, and an animal born by caesarean section, and an animal that is a tumtum, and a hermaphrodite.
And if you would say: Here too, omit from this baraita a tumtum, then there are only four types of animals listed in the baraita.
messages.quote: There are five types of animals

messages.text: Remove the mention of a tumtum and in its place insert an orphan, i.e., an animal born after the death of its mother, which is also disqualified as a sacrifice.

notes.he: דמי להנך שפסולין משנולדו והיכי דמי יתום כדמפרש בשחיטת חולין בפ' שני (דף לח:) שמתה אמו בשעת לידה זה פריש למיתה וזה פריש לחיים:
notes.en: An orphan: it resembles the others that are disqualified from birth. What is an orphan? As explained in Chullin, chapter two (38b): its mother died while giving birth to it; she departed toward death and it toward life.

notes.he: כי ההוא יתום דכי ילדתו אמו היא פירשה למיתה והוא פורש לחיים ומשום הכי לא קדיש כדגמרינן בהשוחט תחת אמו פרט ליתום:
notes.en: Remove the tumtum and insert the orphan: like the orphan whose mother, as she bore it, departed toward death while it departed toward life, and therefore it is not sacred, as we learn from “one who slaughters in place of its mother”: to exclude an orphan.

messages.caption: Seven challenges to Rav Ḥisda: six times “omit the tumtum,” and once “swap it for an orphan.”

messages.text: Let us say that this question of whether a tumtum is a distinct entity or is definitely either a male or female is the subject of a dispute between tanna’im. As it is taught in a baraita that

notes.he: הא דרב חסדא דאיכא דס"ל ספק הוי:
notes.en: Let us say it is a dispute of tanna’im: Rav Ḥisda’s view, since there is one who holds it is an uncertainty.

notes.he: הא מילתא דרב חסדא דאיכא למ"ד דטומטום קדוש מספיקא ואיכא למ"ד שמא בריה הוי ולא קדיש:
notes.en: Let us say it is a dispute of tanna’im: Rav Ḥisda’s statement. One view holds a tumtum is sacred out of uncertainty, and another holds that perhaps it is a creature of its own kind and not sacred.

messages.text: A hermaphrodite is a firstborn, and it comes with its blemish;
It is not imbued with sanctity.
The verse states: “Males” (Deuteronomy 15:19), and wherever it is stated: Male,” this serves to exclude only a tumtum and a hermaphrodite.

Since according to Rabbi Shimon ben Yehuda it is necessary for a verse to exclude a tumtum, like a hermaphrodite, from the category of a male, evidently in his opinion a tumtum is not considered to be one whose status as a male is uncertain but a distinct entity.

And if you would say: Here too, omit from this baraita a tumtum, then the opinion of Rabbi Shimon ben Yehuda is the same as that of the Rabbis, as they too maintain that a hermaphrodite is not sacred.

Rather, is it not that the difference between them is with regard to the status of a tumtum, as the first tanna, i.e., the Rabbis, holds: It is not imbued with sanctity, and they are referring specifically to a hermaphrodite, which was the subject of Rabbi Ilai’s statement, but a tumtum is an uncertain case, and therefore it is sacred due to uncertainty. And Rabbi Shimon…

notes.dh: ואתא ר"ש בן רבי יהודה משום ר"ש למימר טומטום נמי בריה הוא
notes.he: משמע הכא דקסבר אנדרוגינוס בריה הוא כמו טעמא דטומטום ואפי' דמסיק נמי דטומטום ממעט לדידיה מטעם שהוא נקבה כשמטיל מים במקום נקבות מ"מ באנדרוגינוס הוי לעולם משום דבריה הוא ותימה דפ' הערל (יבמות דף פא.) משמע דר"ש חשיב ליה ודאי זכר לר' יוחנן דאמר התם אף מאכילה בחזה ושוק וי"ל דאפי' הוי ודאי זכר ממעטינא ליה זכר אבל נקבה ודאי מימעטא מן טומטום המטיל מים במקום נקבות לפי המסקנא דאפי' ודאי נקבה הוי כיון דלא חייש שמא נהפכה זכרות לנקבות:
notes.en: And Rabbi Shimon ben Yehuda comes to say, in the name of Rabbi Shimon, that a tumtum too is a creature of its own kind: this implies he holds a hermaphrodite is a creature of its own kind for the same reason. Even though the Gemara concludes that for him a tumtum that urinates from the female place is excluded as female, a hermaphrodite is still always a creature of its own kind. It is puzzling, since in Yevamot (81a) it appears that Rabbi Shimon considers it a definite male, according to Rabbi Yoḥanan there. One may answer that even if it were a definite male, he would exclude it by the word “male,” while a tumtum that urinates from the female place is excluded, by the conclusion here, as a definite female, since he is not concerned that the male organ was inverted.

messages.text: …ben Yehuda comes to say: A tumtum is not of uncertain status, but a distinct entity, and it is not sacred at all.

No, everyone agrees with regard to the statement that a tumtum is a distinct entity that there is no doubt that this is incorrect. Where there is doubt is with regard to whether it is a male or a female.

notes.he: דתיקום לרב חסדא כתנאי דתימא ההוא תנא דסבירא ליה בריה הוא סבירא ליה כרבנן בתראי אלא הני תנאי דברייתא בהכי פליגי דכ"ע מטיל במקום זכרות זכר הוי וקדוש:
notes.en: Everyone agrees a tumtum is not in doubt as a creature of its own kind: so you cannot make Rav Ḥisda a dispute of tanna’im by saying the tanna who holds it is a creature of its own kind follows the latter Rabbis. Rather, these tanna’im of the baraita disagree about this: all agree that if it urinates from the male place it is a male and sacred,

notes.he: בזכר או נקבה הוא דמספקא דלא ידעינן אי נקרע שמא הוי זכר ודאי או נקבה ודאית:
notes.en: The doubt is whether it is male or female: we do not know whether, if it is torn open, it will be a definite male or a definite female.

messages.text: In addition, in a case where the tumtum urinates from the place of the male sex organ, then everyone agrees that it is a male. When they disagree is in the case of a tumtum that urinates from the place of the female sex organ.

notes.dh: כי פליגי במטיל מים במקום נקבות
notes.he: והשתא הא דאמר רב חסדא לעיל אבל טומטום דברי הכל ספיקא הוא על כרחך לא אמרו במטיל מים במקום זכרות דההוא ודאי זכר הוא אבל במטיל מים במקום נקבות ואליבא דת"ק אבל ר"ש דלית ליה שום ספיקא בטומטום דאי הוה מטיל מים במקום נקבות הוי נקבה ודאי וא"ת ומנ"ל לרב חסדא דלרבנן בתראי קדוש מספיקא דילמא סברי כר"ש ולא קדוש כלל וי"ל כיון דמההוא טעמא דפליגי באנדרוגינוס משום דבריה הוא לא מצי פליגי בטומטום דלרב חסדא לשום תנא לא הוי בריה מסתמא מודו לת"ק בטומטום דכי קדוש הוא מספיקא כמו שמודה לו רבי ישמעאל וא"ת לקמן פ"ט (בכורות דף נז.) דממעט ר"ש בן יהודה טומטום ואנדרוגינוס ממעשר בהמה משום דממעט בקדשים הזכר ודאי ונקבה ודאית ויליף מעשר מתחת תחת מקדשים מה ענין זה אצל זה הא בקדשים אימעט מכלל זכר מטעם שהוא נקבה כשמטיל מים במקום נקבות אבל מעשר אין חילוק בין זכר ונקבה וי"ל דרב חסדא אומר סמי מכאן טומטום וכן ר"ל דבסמוך:
notes.en: When they disagree is where it urinates from the female place: so Rav Ḥisda’s “a tumtum, all agree, is an uncertainty” cannot refer to one that urinates from the male place, which is certainly male, but to one that urinates from the female place, and according to the first tanna; whereas Rabbi Shimon has no uncertainty about a tumtum at all. You might ask: how does Rav Ḥisda know that for the latter Rabbis it is sacred out of uncertainty; perhaps they hold like Rabbi Shimon and it is not sacred at all? One may answer that since they disagree about the hermaphrodite because it is a creature of its own kind, they cannot disagree about a tumtum, which for Rav Ḥisda no tanna considers a creature of its own kind; presumably they agree with the first tanna that it is sacred out of uncertainty, as Rabbi Yishmael does. And as for 57a, where Rabbi Shimon ben Yehuda excludes a tumtum from animal tithe by comparison with offerings, though tithe draws no line between male and female: Rav Ḥisda says “omit the tumtum from here,” and so does Reish Lakish below.

notes.dh: ואי מטיל מים במקום זכרות דכ"ע לא פליגי דזכר הוא
notes.he: (דאי) דמקום זכרות דבהמה מרוחק הוא ממקום נקבות:
notes.en: If it urinates from the male place, all agree it is a male, since in an animal the male place is far from the female place.

messages.text: One Sage, the Rabbis, holds that we are concerned that perhaps its male sex organ was inverted toward its female sex organ; therefore, it is of uncertain status. And one Sage, Rabbi Shimon ben Yehuda, holds that we are not concerned about this possibility; rather, it is definitely a female. And Rabbi Shimon ben Yehuda maintains in accordance with that which Rabbi Elazar ruled:

notes.dh: ות"ק סבר חיישינן שמא נהפכה זכרותו
notes.he: נכפל גידו מבפנים ומוציא מים במקום שרגיל נקבות להיות נקבה ור"ש סבר לא אמרינן הכי אלא ודאי נקבה הוא והא דאמר רב חסדא טומטום דברי הכל ספק הוא הא אתא לאשמועינן דלא תימא לרבנן בתראי טומטום נמי בריה הוא ולא תהא קדושת בכור חלה על שום טומטום ומיהו ס"ל לרב חסדא איכא תנא דאפילו ספק לית ליה דאי מטיל מים במקום זכרות זכר ואם במקום נקבות נקבה ודכולי עלמא אית להו דרב חסדא דקדושה חלה על טומטום:
notes.en: and the first tanna holds we are concerned that perhaps its male organ was inverted: folded inside, so that it passes water where a female’s would be. Rabbi Shimon holds we do not say so; it is certainly a female. Rav Ḥisda’s “a tumtum, all agree, is an uncertainty” comes to teach that you should not say that for the latter Rabbis a tumtum too is a creature of its own kind and firstborn sanctity takes effect on no tumtum at all. Still, Rav Ḥisda holds there is a tanna who does not even consider it doubtful: urinating from the male place, it is male; from the female place, female. And all agree with Rav Ḥisda that sanctity does take effect on a tumtum.

notes.dh: כי פליגי במטיל מים ממקום נקבות
notes.he: מר סבר (רבנן) תנא קמא דטומטום ספיקא הוא וקדוש מספיקא סברי חיישינן שמא נהפכה זכרותו והויא במקום נקבותו וזכר הוא ומומו עמו:
notes.en: When they disagree is where it urinates from the female place. One Sage, the first tanna, holds a tumtum is an uncertainty and sacred out of uncertainty, since we are concerned that perhaps its male organ was inverted into the female place, and it is a male with its blemish.

notes.he: ור' שמעון [בן יהודה] סבר כל מקום שנאמר זכר להוציא טומטום ואנדרוגינוס דכי מטיל מים במקום נקבות ודאי נקבה הוא:
notes.en: And Rabbi Shimon [ben Yehuda] holds that wherever “male” is said, it excludes a tumtum and a hermaphrodite, since when it urinates from the female place it is certainly female.

messages.text: With regard to a firstborn animal that urinates from the place where the female sex organ is found, it is non-sacred, as it is certainly a female.

notes.he: כלומר ר"ש בן יהודה כי הך הוראה ס"ל:
notes.en: In accordance with that which Rabbi Ilai ruled: that is, Rabbi Shimon ben Yehuda holds like this ruling. [Rashi’s text reads Rabbi Ilai where ours reads Rabbi Elazar.]

notes.he: ולגבי בכור קאמר דלא קדיש דוודאי נקבה הוא. והא ר' אלעאי אמורא הוא ולאו היינו האי דברייתא דאיירי לעיל משום רבי ישמעאל:
notes.en: Non-sacred: he says this of a firstborn, that it is not sacred, since it is certainly female. This Rabbi Ilai is an Amora, not the one in the baraita above who spoke in the name of Rabbi Yishmael.

notes.he: כי הא דהורה ר' אלעזר (ר' אילעאי) לא חיישינן שמא נהפך זכרותו לנקבותו אלא ודאי נקבה הוא:
notes.en: Like that which Rabbi Elazar (Rabbi Ilai) ruled: we are not concerned that perhaps its male organ was inverted toward its female organ; it is certainly female.

messages.text: Who is the Sage who is not concerned about the opinion of the first tanna in the mishna and about the opinion of Rabbi Yishmael, who maintain that a tumtum is a case of uncertainty?
messages.lead: Rabbi Yoḥanan wondered about this ruling of Rabbi Elazar:

notes.he: בהך הוראה דר' אלעאי:
notes.en: Rabbi Yoḥanan wondered: about this ruling of Rabbi Ilai.

notes.he: דמתני' דאמרי טומטום אינו נשחט לא במקדש ולא במדינה משום דספיקא הוא ור' ישמעאל לא פליגי אלא באנדרוגינוס דנעשה נקבות שלו חריץ:
notes.en: Neither the first tanna nor Rabbi Yishmael of our mishna: they say a tumtum is slaughtered neither in the Temple nor in the country because it is an uncertainty; and Rabbi Yishmael disagrees only about the hermaphrodite, whose female organ counts as a crack.

notes.he: מאן האי דהכי הורה ולא חש לא לת"ק ולא לר' ישמעאל דמתניתין. כדאמרינן לת"ק בשלמא טומטום במדינה לא דילמא זכר הוא ולית בה מומא ור' ישמעאל סבר זכר ומומו עמו הוא:
notes.en: Rabbi Yoḥanan wondered: who is this who ruled so, without concern for the first tanna or for Rabbi Yishmael of our mishna? As we said, for the first tanna, granted, a tumtum may not be slaughtered in the country, since perhaps it is a male without a blemish; and Rabbi Yishmael holds it is a male with its blemish.

messages.text: And let Rabbi Yoḥanan also say: Who is this who is not concerned about the opinion of the latter Rabbis in the mishna, as Rav Ḥisda says: This dispute refers to a hermaphrodite; but with regard to a tumtum, everyone agrees that it is an uncertain case.
Rabbi Yoḥanan does not hold in accordance with that statement of Rav Ḥisda; rather, he maintains that according to the latter Rabbis a tumtum is a distinct entity.

notes.he: דרב חסדא אלא רבנן בתראי אטומטום נמי אמרי דבריה הוא:
notes.en: Rabbi Yoḥanan does not hold like Rav Ḥisda: rather, the latter Rabbis say of a tumtum too that it is a creature of its own kind.

notes.he: לא סבירא ליה הא דרב חסדא א"כ הא דאמר דהורה כרבנן הורה דאמרי אינו בכור ויוצא לחולין ליגזז:
notes.en: He does not hold like Rav Ḥisda. [A later editor suggests reading: if he does not hold like Rav Ḥisda, let him say that he ruled, etc.] If so, he ruled like the Rabbis, who say it is not a firstborn and becomes non-sacred, to be shorn.

messages.text: If Rabbi Yoḥanan does not hold in accordance with Rav Ḥisda, why did he wonder about Rabbi Elazar’s ruling? Let him say that Rabbi Elazar said his opinion in accordance with the opinion of the latter Rabbis.

notes.he: אמאי קא מתמה הא ר' אילעאי הוא דאמר כרבנן בתראי:
notes.en: If he does not hold so, why does he wonder? Rabbi Ilai ruled like the latter Rabbis.

messages.text: That is indeed what he is saying: Who is the Sage who leaves aside the opinion of two Sages, the first tanna and Rabbi Yishmael, and acts in accordance with one opinion, the latter Rabbis?

notes.he: ת"ק ור' ישמעאל ועביד כחד רבנן בתראי:
notes.en: Leaves two, the first tanna and Rabbi Yishmael, and acts like one, the latter Rabbis.

notes.he: הכי נמי קאמר ר' יוחנן דתהי עליה מאן שביק תרי ת"ק ור' ישמעאל והורי כחד כרבנן:
notes.en: That is indeed what Rabbi Yoḥanan says in wondering about him: who leaves two, the first tanna and Rabbi Yishmael, and rules like one, the Rabbis?

messages.text: And Rabbi Elazar, in accordance with whose opinion does he hold?
He holds in accordance with that which Reish Lakish says:

The Sages said that the halakhic status of a tumtum is an uncertain case only with regard to a person, since the male sex organ and the female sex organ are in one place, i.e., a man and a woman urinate from the same area of the body. Since that area is concealed in the case of a tumtum, its status is uncertain. But with regard to a tumtum animal, there is no uncertainty whether it is a male or a female, as the genitals of a male and a female are not found in the same place. Rather, if it urinates from the place of the male sex organ, it is a male; if it urinates from the place of the female sex organ, it is a female.

notes.he: וליכא למיבדקינהו בהטלת מים [אבל] בבהמה אין בה שום ספק לדברי הכל והאי דקאמר ת"ק דמתניתין אינו נשחט במטיל מים במקום זכרות קאמר דודאי קדוש הילכך אינו נשחט במדינה ובמקדש נמי לא חזי להקרבה דנראה כבעל מום לפי שאין לו זכרות דהא ממעטינן ליה מהקרבה בכמה דוכתי הזכר ולא טומטום ורבי ישמעאל אאנדרוגינוס קאי ורבנן בתראי אאנדרוגינוס קיימי אבל טומטום כולי עלמא מודו דמטיל מים במקום זכרות זכר במקום נקבות נקבה ור' אילעאי אליבא דכולהו הורה:
notes.en: Since its male and female organs are in one place: they cannot be checked by urination. [But] in an animal there is no doubt at all, according to everyone. When the first tanna of our mishna says it is not slaughtered, he means one that urinates from the male place, which is certainly sacred: so it is not slaughtered in the country, and in the Temple too it is unfit, since it looks blemished, with no visible male organ, as we exclude it from offerings in several places: “the male, and not a tumtum.” Rabbi Yishmael speaks of the hermaphrodite, and the latter Rabbis too speak of the hermaphrodite; but about a tumtum all agree: urinating from the male place, male; from the female place, female. And Rabbi Ilai ruled according to all of them.

notes.dh: לא אמרו טומטום ספק אלא באדם
notes.he: כר"ש בר' יהודה דסבירא ליה ולאו אליבא דכולי עלמא קאמר דפשיטא לת"ק דמתני' דספיקא הוא דאין שוחטין לא במקדש ולא במדינה:
notes.en: They said a tumtum is an uncertainty only in a person: he holds like Rabbi Shimon ben Yehuda, and does not say this according to everyone, since for the first tanna of our mishna it is obviously an uncertainty, for he says it is slaughtered neither in the Temple nor in the country.

notes.dh: ור' אילעאי דאורי כר"ל נמי סברה דאמר ריש לקיש כו'
notes.he: במקום א' קרוב זה אצל זה:
notes.en: And Rabbi Ilai, who ruled like Reish Lakish, also holds as Reish Lakish said: in one place, close to each other.

messages.text: And let us be concerned that perhaps its male sex organ was turned round to the place of its female sex organ.
messages.quote: if it urinates from the place of the female sex organ, it is a female

notes.he: בין לר' אילעאי בין לריש לקיש וליחוש כו':
notes.en: Rav Oshaya objects, both to Rabbi Ilai and to Reish Lakish: let us be concerned, etc.

messages.text: @Rav Oshaya In accordance with whose opinion do you raise this objection? Is it in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Meir, who is concerned about the minority of cases? The halakha is not in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Meir, and therefore one should follow the majority of animals, to whom this does not occur.

notes.he: בתמיה. כלומר מי חיישינן ליחידאה:
notes.en: Like Rabbi Meir? This is asked in surprise: do we take a lone opinion’s concern into account?

notes.he: א"ל אביי כמאן כלומר את דאמרת וליחוש כר' מאיר סבירא לך דיחידאה הוא דחייש למיעוט גבי קטן וקטנה לא חולצת כו'. כלומר דמיעוט הוו דנהפך זכרות לנקבות:
notes.en: Abaye said to him: like whom? You who said “let us be concerned” hold like Rabbi Meir, who alone is concerned for the minority, as with a minor boy and girl who do not perform ḥalitza. That is, the male organ’s being inverted to the female place is a minority case.

messages.text: You may even say that Rav Oshaya’s objection is in accordance with the opinion of the Rabbis, who are not concerned about a minority. The reason is that since in this case, the animal has changed in that it is different from typical animals, as it is a tumtum, perhaps it is also changed with regard to its male sex organ being inverted toward the female sex organ. If so, the Sages disagree with regard to this principle: There are those who say that since it has changed, it has changed, and there are those who say that the claim that since it has changed, it has changed is not accepted.
messages.lead: Abaye bar Avin and Rav Ḥananya bar Avin both say:

notes.he: נמי פרכינן הכי דהואיל ואישתני לענין טומטום אישתני דנהפכה זכרותו לנקבותו:
notes.en: You may even say the Rabbis: we can raise this challenge for them too, since it has changed in being a tumtum, it has changed, so that its male organ was inverted into its female place.

notes.he: כלומר איכא למ"ד אמרינן הואיל ואישתני אישתני בבהמה דהיינו ת"ק דפליג לעיל עליה דר"ש בן יהודה דלא חייש שמא נהפכה ור' אלעזר כר"ש סבירא ליה:
notes.en: And he answers: there are those who say it has changed. That is, there is a view that in an animal we say “since it has changed, it has changed”: the first tanna above, who disagrees with Rabbi Shimon ben Yehuda and is concerned that it was inverted; and Rabbi Elazar holds like Rabbi Shimon.

notes.he: דפליגי עליה בהא מודו דכיון דאישתני דטומטום הוא אישתני נמי דניחוש דילמא נהפך זכרותו לנקבות:
notes.en: You may even say the Rabbis, who disagree with him on that point, agree here: since it has changed in being a tumtum, it has also changed, and we are concerned that perhaps its male organ was inverted into the female place.

notes.he: אע"ג דאישתני דטומטום הוא לא אישתני נמי זכרותו לנקבות:
notes.en: And there are those who say: although it has changed in being a tumtum, its male organ has not also changed into the female place.

messages.text: Let us say that the question of whether an animal that has changed in one respect has changed in a different respect, or whether it has not changed, is the subject of a dispute between tanna’im. As it is taught in a baraita:

notes.he: אי אמרי' הואיל ואישתני או לא אמרי' תנאי היא:
notes.en: Let us say: whether we say “since it has changed” or not is a dispute of tanna’im.

messages.text: With regard to a tumtum who betrothed a woman, the betrothal is considered a betrothal, due to uncertainty, as the tumtum might be a male; and similarly, if the tumtum was betrothed by a man, the betrothal is deemed a betrothal due to uncertainty, as the tumtum might be a female.

notes.he: לחומרא וצריכה גט שמא זכר הוא:
notes.en: One who betrothed, his betrothal is a betrothal: stringently, and she needs a bill of divorce, since perhaps he is a male.

notes.he: וזה שקדשו אסור בקרובותיו של טומטום כגון באמו ובאחותו דשמא נקבה הוא:
notes.en: Was betrothed, the betrothal is a betrothal: the man who betrothed the tumtum is forbidden to the tumtum’s relatives, such as its mother and sister, since perhaps it is a female.

notes.he: דאסור בקרובותיה וכן אם נתקדש נאסר אותו שקידשו בקרובותיו. וחולץ דשמא זכר הוא:
notes.en: A tumtum who betrothed, the betrothal is a betrothal [a later editor adds: she is forbidden to the tumtum’s relatives and also needs a bill of divorce, as Rashi explains]: he is forbidden to her relatives; and if it was betrothed, the one who betrothed it is forbidden to its relatives. And it performs ḥalitza, since perhaps it is a male.

messages.text: And if the brother of the tumtum died childless, and there is no other brother who can perform levirate marriage with the widow, the tumtum performs ḥalitza, i.e., his brother’s widow removes his shoe, as the tumtum might be a male, and she would require ḥalitza to release her from the levirate bond. And if the tumtum died, one of the brothers of the tumtum performs ḥalitza with the wife of the tumtum, or enters into levirate marriage with the wife of the tumtum, in case the tumtum was a male.

notes.he: לחומרא שאם אין שם אחר אלא הוא בעיא יבמתו חליצה אבל יש שם אחר לא חליץ טומטום דהא האי תנא בנקבה נמי מספקא ליה:
notes.en: And performs ḥalitza: stringently. If there is no brother but the tumtum, the sister-in-law needs its ḥalitza; but if there is another brother, the tumtum does not perform ḥalitza, since this tanna is also uncertain whether it is female.

notes.he: חומרא היא שמא זכר הוא:
notes.en: And they perform ḥalitza with its wife: a stringency, since perhaps it is a male.

notes.he: ממה נפשך אי זכר הוא שפיר מייבם אחיו ואם נקבה הוא אשה בעלמא הוא דנסב האי אחיו של טומטום אבל טומטום לא מייבם דאינו בן לידה ולא קרינא ביה להקים לאחיו שם:
notes.en: And enter into levirate marriage with its wife: either way. If it is a male, his brother properly performs levirate marriage; if it is a female, this brother simply marries a woman. But the tumtum itself does not perform levirate marriage, since it cannot father children, and “to establish a name for his brother” does not apply to it.

notes.he: משום דתנן בהערל בעלה פסלה מפני שהיא בעילת זנות:
notes.en: And it does not perform levirate marriage, as we learned in HaArel: her husband disqualifies her, since it is a promiscuous intercourse.

notes.he: ממה נפשך אי אשתו הויא קיים מצות יבום ואי לאו לא נאסרה עליו:
notes.en: And they perform ḥalitza with its wife and levirate marriage with its wife: either way. If she was his brother’s wife, he has fulfilled the mitzva of levirate marriage; if not, she was not forbidden to him.

messages.text: And it is taught in another baraita:
The wife of a tumtum performs ḥalitza and does not enter into levirate marriage.
With regard to these two baraitot, the Sages assumed that everyone holds in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Akiva, who says:

A eunuch whose condition is caused naturally, i.e., one who was entirely lacking in sexual capacity from birth, does not perform ḥalitza and does not enter into levirate marriage with his sister-in-law, as he is not included in the mitzva of levirate marriage. Likewise, if he died his brothers do not perform ḥalitza with his wife, and they may not enter into levirate marriage with her, as she is forbidden to them as a brother’s wife who does not require levirate marriage.

notes.he: ביבמות פרק הערל (יבמות דף עט:) סריס חמה לא חולץ ולא מייבם ואשתו לא חולצת ולא מתייבמת שלא היתה לו שעת הכושר:
notes.en: Is it not that everyone holds like Rabbi Akiva, who said in Yevamot, chapter HaArel (79b): a eunuch from birth does not perform ḥalitza or levirate marriage, and his wife does not perform ḥalitza and is not taken in levirate marriage, since he never had a time of fitness.

messages.text: What, is it not that the two baraitot disagree about this, that the one who says that a tumtum performs ḥalitza and one of the brothers performs ḥalitza with the wife of the tumtum or enters into levirate marriage with the wife of the tumtum holds that we do not say that since this tumtum has changed from an average person, he might also have changed in that he is a eunuch whose condition is caused naturally, and therefore the brothers would be prohibited from entering into levirate marriage with the wife? Rather, if the tumtum is a male, it is assumed that he is capable of fathering children, and consequently his wife requires levirate marriage.
messages.quote: performs ḥalitza with the wife of the tumtum, or enters into levirate marriage

notes.he: דמ"ד מייבמין לאשתו ממ"נ סבר אי זכר הוא שפיר מייבם דלא אמרינן הואיל ואישתני למיהוי טומטום אישתני נמי לספוקי בסריס חמה שאפילו יקרע וימצא זכר יהא סריס ואשת סריס אין מתייבמת:
notes.en: And this is what they disagree about: the one who says they take its wife in levirate marriage either way holds that if it is a male, his brother properly takes her, since we do not say “since it has changed in being a tumtum, it has also changed” so as to doubt whether it is a eunuch from birth, such that even if torn and found male it would be a eunuch, and a eunuch’s wife is not taken in levirate marriage.

notes.he: לא אמרינן הואיל ואישתני דהוה טומטום אישתני נמי דהוה סריס חמה אלא לא הוי סריס חמה וצריכה אשתו חליצה או יבום:
notes.en: We do not say “since it has changed in being a tumtum, it has also changed in being a eunuch from birth.” It is not a eunuch from birth, and its wife needs ḥalitza or levirate marriage.

messages.text: And the one who says that the wife of a tumtum performs ḥalitza and does not enter into levirate marriage maintains that we say that since this person has changed, he has changed, i.e., the possibility that he might be a eunuch whose condition is caused naturally is considered, and therefore his wife may not enter into levirate marriage.
messages.quote: performs ḥalitza and does not enter into levirate marriage

notes.dh: ומ"ד אין מתייבמת סבר אמרינן הואיל ואישתני
notes.he: למיהוי טומטום אישתני נמי לספוקי למיהוי סריס חמה אפילו ימצא זכר הילכך אין מתייבמת אשתו דנמצאו פוגעים בערוה דכיון דזכר הוא קדושיו קדושין וכיון דסריס חמה הוא אין אשתו זקוקה ליבם הויא כאשת אח שיש לה בנים והמייבמה פוגע באיסור אשת אח ומיהו חליצה בעיא דלא פשיטא לן שהוא סריס דשמא לאו סריס הוא הילכך בעיא חליצה:
notes.en: And the one who says she is not taken in levirate marriage holds we say “since it has changed” in being a tumtum, it has also changed, so that it may be a eunuch from birth even if found male. Therefore its wife is not taken in levirate marriage, lest they encounter a forbidden relation: as a male, its betrothal is valid, and as a eunuch from birth, its wife is not bound to the levir, so she is like a brother’s wife who has children, and one who takes her violates the prohibition of a brother’s wife. Still, she needs ḥalitza, since it is not certain that it is a eunuch.

notes.dh: ומ"ד חולצת ולא מתייבמת סבר דאמרינן הואיל ואישתני אישתני
notes.he: דהוי סריס חמה ואהכי חולצת מספק ולא מתייבם משום דכתיב אשר לא יבנה את בית אחיו ודילמא הא לאו בית אחיו הואי:
notes.en: And the one who says she performs ḥalitza and is not taken in levirate marriage holds we do say “since it has changed, it has changed,” to be a eunuch from birth. So she performs ḥalitza out of doubt, and is not taken in levirate marriage, since it is written “who will not build up his brother’s house,” and perhaps this is not his brother’s house.

messages.text: No; everyone agrees that we say that since this person has changed, he has changed, and there is a concern that he might be a eunuch whose condition is caused naturally. Rather, the difference between the rulings is that this baraita, which permits the wife of the tumtum to enter levirate marriage, is in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Eliezer, who disagrees with Rabbi Akiva and maintains that levirate marriage may be performed with the wife of a eunuch whose condition is caused naturally, and that baraita, which prohibits levirate marriage, is in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Akiva, that the brothers of a eunuch whose condition is caused naturally do not enter into levirate marriage with the wife of the tumtum.

notes.he: ומספקינן ליה בסריס חמה. והא דאמרינן מתייבמת רבי אליעזר היא דאמר בפ' הערל (יבמות דף פ.) אשת סריס חמה מתייבמת שכן במינן מתרפאין באלכסנדריא של מצרים הילכך ממ"נ שרי לייבומה. ומ"ד לא מתייבמת כר"ע:
notes.en: No, all say perhaps it has changed, and we are in doubt whether it is a eunuch from birth. The one who says she is taken in levirate marriage is Rabbi Eliezer, who says in chapter HaArel (Yevamot 80a): the wife of a eunuch from birth is taken in levirate marriage, since such people are healed in Alexandria of Egypt; so either way it is permitted. The one who says she is not follows Rabbi Akiva.

notes.he: והאי דקתני חולצת ומייבמת את אשתו ר' אליעזר [היא] דאמר בפרק הערל (ור' אליעזר אמר) לא כי אלא סריס חולץ וחולצי' לאשתו שיש לו רפואה:
notes.en: The one that teaches “she performs ḥalitza and is taken in levirate marriage” is Rabbi Eliezer, who said in chapter HaArel: not so, a eunuch performs ḥalitza and they perform ḥalitza with his wife, since he can be cured.

notes.he: והא דקתני חולצת ולא מתייבמת ר' עקיבא היא דאמר סריס חמה לא היתה לו שעת הכושר:
notes.en: The one that teaches “she performs ḥalitza and is not taken in levirate marriage” is Rabbi Akiva, who said a eunuch from birth never had a time of fitness.

messages.text: And who is the tanna who holds in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Akiva that the wife of a eunuch whose condition is caused naturally does not require levirate marriage, and yet he maintains that the wife of a tumtum must perform ḥalitza? If we say it is Rabbi Yehuda, this cannot be, as in his opinion even if the genitals of a tumtum were revealed and he was found to be a male, he deems him like a definite eunuch whose condition is caused naturally, and therefore his wife does not require ḥalitza at all.

notes.dh: ומאן האי תנא דאית ליה כר"ע
notes.he: ואמר חולצת ולא מתייבמת:
notes.en: And who is the tanna who holds like Rabbi Akiva and says she performs ḥalitza and is not taken in levirate marriage?

notes.he: לטומטום ואפי' חליצה לא תיבעי דהא ר"ע באשת סריס חמה לא בעי חליצה:
notes.en: He makes the tumtum a definite eunuch: then even ḥalitza should not be needed, since Rabbi Akiva does not require ḥalitza for the wife of a eunuch from birth.

notes.he: כלומר כמאן מתלמידי ר' עקיבא אתייא הא דחולצת ולא מתייבמת דכר' עקיבא גופיה לא מיתוקמא דהא איהו אמר סריס חמה לא חולץ ולא חולצין אילימא כר' יהודה תלמידו דר' עקיבא איהו ודאי סריס חמה משוי ליה ואמאי חולצת דתנן ר' יהודה אמר כו':
notes.en: And who is the tanna following Rabbi Akiva? That is, which of Rabbi Akiva’s students stands behind “she performs ḥalitza and is not taken in levirate marriage”? It cannot be Rabbi Akiva himself, who said a eunuch from birth does not perform ḥalitza and they do not perform ḥalitza with his wife. If we say Rabbi Yehuda, his student, he certainly makes it a eunuch from birth, so why would she perform ḥalitza? As we learned: Rabbi Yehuda says, etc.

messages.text: As we learned in a mishna:

With regard to a tumtum who was torn open so that his genitals were exposed, and he was found to be a male, he must not perform ḥalitza, because he is treated like a eunuch whose condition is caused naturally.
Just as this tumtum does not perform ḥalitza, so too, his widow does not require ḥalitza.

Rather, it is the opinion of Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda, who maintains that if a tumtum was torn open and he was found to be a male, he is considered as a matter of uncertainty to be a eunuch whose condition is caused naturally, and consequently his wife requires ḥalitza. As it is taught in a baraita that

notes.he: דשמא קאמר הילכך חליצה בעיא דשמא זכר הוא ושמא אינו סריס ולא מתייבמת דשמא זכר הוא וסריס הוא ואינה זקוקה ליבם ונמצא פוגע באשת אח שיש לה בנים:
notes.en: Rather, Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda, who says “perhaps.” So she needs ḥalitza, since perhaps it is a male and perhaps not a eunuch; and she is not taken in levirate marriage, since perhaps it is a male and a eunuch, she is not bound to the levir, and he would encounter a brother’s wife who has children.

messages.text: A tumtum does not perform ḥalitza with the wife of his late, childless brother if there are other brothers to perform ḥalitza, as perhaps the skin covering his genitals will be torn open and he will be found to be a eunuch whose condition is caused naturally, and the widow would not be released from the levirate bond by his ḥalitza.

notes.he: ובמקום אחין קאמר דלא יחלוץ (וליחוש) שמא סריס חמה הוא אבל אין שם אחר יחלוץ ולא מיפטרא יבמתו בולא כלום דשמא לאו סריס הוא הילכך אשתו נמי בעיא חליצה שמא לאו סריס הוא ולא מתייבמת דשמא סריס הוא:
notes.en: Perhaps it will be torn, etc.: he speaks of a case where there are other brothers, that the tumtum should not perform ḥalitza, lest it be a eunuch from birth. But if there is no other, it performs ḥalitza, and its sister-in-law is not left without any release, since perhaps it is not a eunuch. Therefore its wife too needs ḥalitza, since perhaps it is not a eunuch, and she is not taken in levirate marriage, since perhaps it is.

notes.he: תלמידיה הוא דתניא וכו'. וכיון דשמא ימצא סריס חמה ולא ודאי משום הכי חולצת:
notes.en: Rather, Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda, his student, as it is taught, etc. Since perhaps it will be found a eunuch from birth, but not certainly, she performs ḥalitza.

messages.text: According to this opinion, it is not certain that a tumtum would be found to be a eunuch whose condition is caused naturally.

messages.caption: Two baraitot on the tumtum’s widow, and whose view each follows.

messages.text: Why does this individual not perform ḥalitza due only to the possibility that he will be found to be a eunuch whose condition is caused naturally? Is that to say that every tumtum whose skin was torn is found to be a male and is not found to be a female?
messages.quote: perhaps the skin covering his genitals will be torn open

notes.he: דלא מספקא ליה אלא בסריס חמה ובנקבה לא מספקא ליה:
notes.en: Is that to say every tumtum that is torn open is found to be male, so that he is in doubt only about a eunuch from birth and not about a female?

messages.text: Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda, said his opinion in the formulation of: Perhaps, which includes multiple uncertainties: A tumtum must not perform ḥalitza, as perhaps he will be torn open and found to be a female, who can certainly not perform ḥalitza.
Alternatively, if he is found to be a male, he may also not perform ḥalitza, since perhaps he will be found to be a eunuch whose condition is caused naturally.
Since both Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda, agree that a tumtum may not perform ḥalitza for his brother’s wife, what is the practical difference between their opinions?

notes.he: בין רבי יהודה לר' יוסי בטומטום שמת אחיו הא תרוייהו לא יחלוץ קאמרי:
notes.en: What is the difference between them: between Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Yosei, regarding a tumtum whose brother died, since both say it does not perform ḥalitza.

notes.he: בין לר' יהודה דאמר ודאי סריס חמה הוי ובין לר' יוסי דאמר ספק מיכדי בין מר ובין מר לא חולץ קאמר אמר רבא לפסול במקום אחין וליחלוץ שלא במקום אחים איכא בינייהו. לר' יהודה דאמר שמא ימצא סריס חמה פוסל במקום אחים שאם עשה בה מאמר אמרינן דילמא לאו סריס הוא ופסלה על האחין וכן נמי אי ליכא אחין אלא הוא חולץ. ולר' יהודה דאמר שהוא כסריס לא פסל במקום אחין ולא חולץ שלא במקום אחין. והאי דקאמר ר' יוסי טומטום לא חולץ היינו במקום אחין אבל שלא במקום אחין חולץ:
notes.en: [This note runs into Rava’s answer on 43a.] What is the difference between Rabbi Yehuda, who says it is certainly a eunuch from birth, and Rabbi Yosei, who says it is a doubt, when both say it does not perform ḥalitza? Rava said: whether it disqualifies her where there are brothers, and performs ḥalitza where there are none. For Rabbi Yosei [the text reads Rabbi Yehuda; the sense requires Rabbi Yosei], who says perhaps it will be found a eunuch from birth, it disqualifies her where there are brothers: if it made a levirate betrothal with her, we say perhaps it is not a eunuch, and it has disqualified her for the brothers; and if there are no brothers, it performs ḥalitza. For Rabbi Yehuda, who says it is like a eunuch, it neither disqualifies her where there are brothers nor performs ḥalitza where there are none. And when Rabbi Yosei says a tumtum does not perform ḥalitza, he means where there are brothers; where there are none, it does.

notes.he: סליק פירקא
notes.en: The chapter is concluded. [It ends with Rava’s answer on 43a.]
